title: Remix Rules
summary: Project rules for Remix: route loaders and actions, nested routes, error boundaries, validated forms and progressive enhancement.
description: These rules keep an agent working with the platform in Remix: data in loaders, writes in actions and forms that submit even before JavaScript loads.
They also set expectations for nested routes and error boundaries so failures stay local to one section of a page instead of taking down the whole screen.
useWhen: You add routes to a Remix app with an agent
Components fetch data with effects instead of loaders
A failed request blanks the whole page
Forms rely on client-side state only
body:
# Project rules: Remix

## Routes and data
- Each route file owns its data. Read data in `loader`, change data in `action`, and read it in the component with `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()`. Do not fetch initial data in `useEffect`.
- Use nested routes and `<Outlet />` for shared layouts. Name files with the flat-route dot convention and use pathless layouts for shared chrome.
- Return responses with `json` or plain objects, set `headers` for caching on the loader, and keep loaders fast; load independent data in parallel with `Promise.all` or defer slow data.

## Mutations
- Use `<Form>` for navigation-style submits and `useFetcher` for in-place updates. Forms must work without JavaScript.
- Validate form data on the server in the action with Zod, and return field errors with a 400 status; show them next to the inputs. Redirect after a successful write.
- Protect actions and loaders: check the session first and throw a redirect or a 401 response.

## Errors and UI state
- Export an `ErrorBoundary` from every route that can fail, and use `isRouteErrorResponse` to tell expected errors (404, 403) from crashes. Throw `Response` objects for expected cases.
- Use `useNavigation` for pending UI and optimistic updates.

## Server-only code
- Keep database and secrets in `*.server.ts` files so they never reach the client bundle.

## Before finishing
- Run `tsc`, the linter, the tests and `remix build`. Test loaders and actions as plain functions.

example.prompt: Add an edit form for a project name with validation
example.result: The agent adds an action that parses with Zod and returns 400 with field errors, a Form with a pending state, a redirect on success, an ErrorBoundary and a test of the action function.

faq.question: Why keep forms working without JavaScript?
faq.answer: Remix submits a normal form post first and enhances it later, so the feature survives slow loads and script failures.

faq.question: Does this cover React Router framework mode?
faq.answer: Mostly yes, since Remix merged into it. Check file naming and import paths against your version.

access: Instructions for the agent only; no commands or network use of its own
